target_customer: Software engineers and data teams who run Postgres and need analytics on event and time series data
problem: Analytics queries on row based Postgres are slow, forcing teams to stand up a separate warehouse.
business_model: Open source Postgres extensions with a hosted serverless analytics cloud

founders.name: Joseph Sciarrino
founders.background_notes: A cofounder known as JD is mentioned in the launch post without a full name.

competitors.name: Citus Columnar
competitors.what: Open source columnar storage access method for Postgres that Hydra forked
competitors.funding_then: Part of Microsoft owned Citus Data

technical_complexity.rationale: Building columnar storage, vectorized execution and later compute and storage separation inside the Postgres extension model is database engine work for a six person team.

defensibility.rationale: Core code was open source and forked from Citus Columnar, so copying was possible, and the later pg_duckdb extension was MIT licensed and co-developed with DuckDB Labs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it early; Supabase absorbed the team and maintainership in February 2026.

market_need_then: Postgres was already widely adopted by developers, and the founders chose it as a base for that reason, but dated demand evidence is thin.

branding.domain_note: Hosted product at hydra.so; documentation at docs.hydras.io. The .so domain suggests the exact .com was not used.
branding.community_and_virality: Show HN posts for Hydra 1.0 in 2023 and 2025 Reddit threads discussing the product.

brand_strength.rationale: Reasonable developer attention through Show HN and the pg_duckdb project, but no sourced evidence of brand pull.

outcome_analysis: Hydra raised a 3.1 million seed after Demo Day and built open source columnar Postgres, later co-developing the pg_duckdb extension with DuckDB Labs, which also took a stake in 2024. Supabase announced in February 2026 that the team was joining to lead its Open Warehouse Architecture work. Terms were undisclosed, and one community comment called the older columnar extension abandoned, so the exit looks like a team and maintainership move rather than a revenue story.
notes: TechCrunch and Hydra's About page both say 3.1M; the exact month is not given (right after Demo Day). A third party profile lists 3.6M total, unverified. hydra.so could not be fetched (DNS failure); product details from YC page and search. Citus Columnar fork date is from a Hacker News comment, so the competitor date is approximate.
